propositions: Errored pairs are incorrectly counted as decision flips in the parity metric because the flip comparison at parity.py:107 lacks an errored guard, treating synthetic errored decisions as model verdicts.

A single transient infrastructure error (e.g., throttle) fails the parity quality gate as a fabricated decision flip, rejecting a slot as a spurious model regression when criterion (b) demands zero flips.

The fix excludes pairs where either side has errored=True from decision_flips, counts them into a new errored_pairs metric, and surfaces that in the gating string so distinct error scenarios are distinguishable.

Errored pairs must not be scored under criterion (b) because parity.py:46 documents errored as not a model verdict, and criterion (d) already gates error rate separately, making flip-counting a double violation.

An errored side coupled with valid=True produces a silent fabricated flip (flips==1, validity_v2==1.0) with no corroborating error-rate signal, proving arm-level error rate cannot retroactively localize or exclude fabricated flips.
